title: MIRROR: Make Your Object-Level Multi-View Generation More Consistent with Training-Free Rectification
summary: Four demonstrated defects affect core TTM/FRM theory: incorrect depth origin in Eq. 4; invalid feature-to-coordinate inequality in Eq. 15; nonvanishing Jacobian-omission error for the unregularized dual-anchor loss; and false fusion composition law. Empirical improvements and ablations remain positive evidence for tested settings.
limitations: No acquired author repository; historical implementation choices are unknown.
Separate supplement availability is undetermined after the supplied HTTP 403 access failure.
No author-code execution, model sampling, timing reproduction, or fresh empirical validation.
All 28 pages read as text; selected critical equations and figures visually inspected, not every gallery image.
Constructed counterexamples test printed mathematical definitions; no empirical score loss is inferred.

claim.location: PDF p. 5, Definition 4.1 and Eq. (4), Depth Prior Estimation
claim.text: The stated camera-centered depth formula tracks corresponding points under a fixed-elevation camera orbit.

assumptions: Level circular look-at cameras; visible pivot marker; common principal point 100; distance 4; compatible scale; azimuth change pi/6.
Depth follows the paper's stated camera-center distance convention.
problems.check: A pivot marker projects to the principal point in both views; Eq. (4) instead predicts 98 from 100.
problems.result: The printed transform gives a two-unit displacement for an invariant image point.
counterevidence: Object-centered depth and orthographic coordinates could give a restricted repaired formula.
No acquired code establishes whether a missing centering step was implemented.
Reported image metrics can improve despite biased correspondence.
problems.impact: Core TTM coordinates determine feature-block selection and rectification.
problems.correction: Specify intrinsics/extrinsics and depth convention, or restrict to centered orthographic geometry with an offset and consistent units.
problems.core_dependency: TTM coordinates select feature blocks and rectification correspondences.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: camera-centered pivot depth produces a two-unit motion where the pivot image coordinate must remain fixed.

acceptance_check.scope: Restricted centered orthographic repair requires explicit depth/intrinsics conventions; no empirical-image failure inferred.

claim.location: PDF p. 5 Proposition 4.2/Eq. (5); p. 13 Appendix B.1/Eq. (15); Eq. (19)
claim.text: A transformed-image difference is bounded by transformed-coordinate displacement and depth-estimation error.

assumptions: T_alpha is the declared image/feature operator on L2.
alpha=0, x0=phi, xhat0=1.1 phi, ||phi||2=1; constant, bounded-gradient depth estimator.
problems.check: T0 is identity: feature error squared 0.01 while coordinate displacement is zero.
problems.result: Eq. (15)'s first inequality is false. This refutes the proof step, not identity-operator stability.
counterevidence: Coordinate-only stability can follow from a Lipschitz depth estimator.
Additional image and warp regularity may support a revised theorem.
problems.impact: Invalid bridge from diffusion error to core TTM feature stability; frozen algorithm depth also differs from varying estimator in proof.
problems.correction: Distinguish coordinates from features; specify fixed depth, spatial regularity, distortion/visibility controls and residual bias; prove the resulting operator bound.
problems.core_dependency: Bridge from diffusion approximation error to TTM feature stability.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: alpha=0 identity case has feature error .01 with zero coordinate displacement, refuting the proof inequality.

acceptance_check.scope: Coordinate stability and favorable trajectories do not establish the printed feature bound; additional operator regularity needed.

claim.location: PDF p. 7 Theorem 4.4/Eq. (13), Eq. (14); pp. 14-15 Appendix B.3; Eqs. (7)-(11) p. 6
claim.text: Omitting the noise-predictor Jacobian has gradient error tending to zero as t tends to zero.

assumptions: Current clean feature u=(sigma,0), sigma=sqrt(1-alpha)>0; adjacent blocks have seven e1 and two e2, all four corners e1.
Local derivative holds adjacent features fixed, matching the p. 6 local gradient map.
Functional input family under printed assumptions, not shown to be a complete sampling trajectory of a particular trained denoiser.
problems.check: Analytic cosine derivative gives error_y tending to P(1-P)(A-B)=0.04025658183577668; centered finite difference confirms the gradient.
problems.result: Under the printed assumptions, vanishing gradient error fails without anchor-norm or loss-gradient control, despite bounded denoiser Jacobian and nonzero finite-noise anchors.
counterevidence: Figs. 10-11 show small errors and similar tested outputs.
An anchor-norm lower bound, cosine regularization or detached weights changes the construction and needs explicit assumptions.
A trajectory-restricted claim would require explicit loss-gradient control along the actual trajectory; the constructed full trajectory has not been established.
problems.impact: Theorem 4.4 directly justifies Eq. (14)'s shortcut; its unconditional guarantee is invalid.
problems.correction: Use the chain-rule operator-norm bound; require uniform Jacobian and loss-gradient bounds with alpha tending to one; separately control finite-step and accumulated effects.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem 4.4 justifies omission of the denoiser Jacobian in core acceleration.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: unregularized cosine functional family has nonvanishing error 0.04025658 with bounded denoiser Jacobian.

acceptance_check.scope: Functional counterexample under printed assumptions, not demonstrated full trained-sampler trajectory. A sufficient trajectory-restricted guarantee controls (sigma/sqrt(alpha))*||J||*||gradient L|| tending to zero; uniform factor bounds suffice but are not necessary.

claim.location: PDF p. 6 after Definition 4.3; pp. 15-16 Proposition B.2/Eqs. (29)-(30)
claim.text: (M T_alpha1)(M T_alpha2)=M T_(alpha1+alpha2) for all angles.

assumptions: Positive collinear features Z=1+x^2+y^2 on a local image interior.
Actual dual-anchor weights become 1/9; after fusion directions remain the same.
problems.check: Exact rational arithmetic gives MZ(0)=7/3 and M^2 Z(0)=11/3.
problems.result: Eq. (29) implies false idempotence; feature/coordinate separation cannot remove M.
counterevidence: Ordinary 3D rotation group law is valid.
The heuristic adjacent-view loss may be useful without the composition theorem.
problems.impact: Invalid explicit homomorphism justification for the core adjacent operator.
problems.correction: Remove the claim or prove a restricted result with explicit projection/idempotence and equivariance assumptions.
problems.core_dependency: Explicit homomorphism argument for the adjacent-view fusion operator.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: zero angles force false idempotence; actual positive-collinear uniform fusion gives 7/3 versus 11/3.

acceptance_check.scope: Ordinary rotations and useful empirical local loss are not refuted; a restricted composition law needs projection/equivariance assumptions.
